page: Amazon Web Services r8i.xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz and includes a 480 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or a GPU, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a mixture of average and weak performance profiles. Single-core CPU performance is average, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2109.87 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1890.0. However, multi-core performance is weak, as indicated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 4363.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 4286.46. Memory bandwidth benchmarks are consistently weak, with uncached read-only large block speeds at 31.47 GB/sec and write speeds at 17.95 GB/sec. Despite these limitations, the instance demonstrates strong performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 33.41 GB/sec and Geekbench text processing at 2742.0.

In terms of workload fit, the r8i.xlarge is configured for memory-intensive tasks that do not require high multi-core compute density or local storage. It supports Redis SET operations at an average rate of 7.49 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 7.9 GB/sec. LLM inference speeds for a small 135M model are average, but drop to a poor 4.56 tokens/second for text generation on a medium 7B model. This profile suggests the instance is suited for caching layers, text processing, and lightweight database operations where memory capacity is prioritized over raw multi-threaded processing power.
